title: CIS Action Reference: Default of Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements)
content:
**CIS action reference card — Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements)**
**Action: `record_agreement_default_c78cb15c` — default of a running agreement**

#### Default
An agreement whose missed-installment entries number at least the tier's default count is in default, and its unbilled balance is billed back at once as a default rebill. A security deposit is never applied and capital credits still payable are never offset at a default, because the service account stays open.

#### When the balance billed back is fixed
The balance billed back at a default is not fixed until the installment due on every bill already issued for the service account carries its installment-billed entry on the agreement's ledger.

Equivalently: so long as a bill already issued for the service account has an installment due on it that has no installment-billed entry on the agreement's ledger, the balance billed back at the default is not yet fixed.

#### What the action does
One call records the default. The agreement's status changes from active to defaulted, with today as its end date; the balance being billed back is added to the arrangement's ledger as a default entry dated today; and the agreement's unbilled balance is closed to zero. Afterwards the agreement shows as defaulted and the default entry shows on its ledger.

#### How it is invoked
Agent-side action. The representative unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and calls `record_agreement_default_c78cb15c` with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

#### Parameters
- `arrangement_id` — reference number of the running payment arrangement that defaults, as returned by the arrangement lookup for the member. Identifier, as shown.
- `rebill_amount` — balance billed back at the default, in US dollars as a positive number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed.

#### Return
A confirmation sentence of the form "Agreement ‹arrangement id› defaulted on ‹YYYY-MM-DD›: ‹amount› USD billed back (entry ‹entry id›); status defaulted." The date is today, the amount carries 2 decimals and the entry id is the reference number of the new ledger entry. Receiving this sentence means the default was recorded.

#### Default count, read off the ledger (hypothetical)
| Tier's default count | Missed-installment entries on the agreement | In default |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | yes |
| 2 | 1 | no |
| 2 | 3 | yes |
